simple.meaning: לָבַט (lâbaṭ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to overthrow ; intransposed, to fall.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Proverbs, Hosea, beginning at Proverbs 10:8. The surrounding contexts include family line, commandment, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָבַט (H3832) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: לָבַט (lâbaṭ) / H3832 is traced through Proverbs 10:8, Proverbs 10:10, Hosea 4:14 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3832. labat [ לָבַט ] verb thrust down, out, or away (Late Hebrew id. ; Arabic strike the ground with a person, i.e. throw one down; Syriac Pa`el incitavit, stimulavit ); — only Niph`al Imperfect be thrust down, away , i.e. ruined; יִלָּבֵט יָבִין לֹא עָם Hosea 4:14 ; יִלָּבֵט שְׂפָתַיִם אֱוִיל Prov 10:8 , 10 . לְבִיָּא לָבִיא לְבִי, see below לבא . לֻבִים see לוּבִים .
